title: Care Gap Analysis and Quality Metrics
summary: Care gaps are evidence-based services that eligible patients haven't received — a missed colorectal cancer screening, an overdue A1C test, a lapsed influenza vaccine. Closing care gaps is central to population health quality programs and value-based contracts.

objectives.text: Define a care gap and explain how they're identified
Describe HEDIS measures and their role in population health
List common strategies for closing care gaps at scale

content_blocks.body: A **care gap** is the difference between a recommended evidence-based service and whether a patient has received it. If a 52-year-old woman with commercial insurance hasn't had a mammogram in 2 years, that's a care gap. If a diabetic patient hasn't had an A1C test in 12 months, that's a care gap.

HEDIS (Healthcare Effectiveness Data and Information Set), maintained by NCQA, is the dominant quality measurement framework in the U.S. Over 90% of health plans report HEDIS measures. Key population health HEDIS measures include:

- **Controlling High Blood Pressure** — % of hypertensive patients with BP < 140/90
- **Comprehensive Diabetes Care** — A1C testing, nephropathy screening, retinal exam, BP control
- **Colorectal Cancer Screening** — colonoscopy, FIT, stool DNA for ages 45–75
- **Breast Cancer Screening** — mammography for women 50–74
- **Well-Child Visits** — pediatric preventive care rates
- **Follow-Up After Hospitalization for Mental Illness** — 7- and 30-day follow-up rates

**Patient outreach.** Automated phone calls, SMS, and patient portal messages for due screenings. Digital-first outreach achieves 15–30% response rates at low cost.

**Point-of-care reminders.** EHR alerts prompt clinicians when eligible patients are due for services during encounters — "Mrs. Smith is due for colorectal cancer screening."

**Opportunistic care.** Closing multiple gaps during a single visit — a patient coming in for a follow-up can get an influenza vaccine and depression screening at the same time.

**Community health workers.** CHWs can conduct in-home screenings, accompany patients to appointments, and address barriers to care like transportation or cost.

**Panel management.** Dedicated staff (care coordinators, panel managers) work the care gap list proactively — reaching out to patients before they experience a health event.
